stories.head: Venus Aerospace raises $91 million amid skepticism
stories.body: Venus Aerospace secured $91 million to advance its rotating detonation rocket engine technology, a concept that sounds more suited for a sci-fi novel than real-world applications. Investors seem to be betting on the potential, despite the technology's unproven status. The funding reflects a willingness to take risks in a sector where the line between ambition and folly is often blurred.
stories.soWhat: This capital injection underscores the appetite for speculative aerospace technologies, even when the odds are long.

stories.head: Space Force welcomes new players to launch program
stories.body: The Space Force has added Relativity and Impulse Space to its national security launch program, a move that could shake up the existing launch landscape. This decision follows a broader trend of integrating smaller, more agile companies into defense contracts, potentially leading to greater innovation—or chaos. With the government opening doors to startups, the competition for launch contracts is set to heat up.
stories.soWhat: This shift indicates that the Space Force is willing to gamble on new entrants, which could either refresh or complicate the launch ecosystem.

stories.head: AST SpaceMobile inches closer to satellite goals
stories.body: AST SpaceMobile launched three more BlueBird satellites, moving closer to its ambitious target of a 45 to 60 satellite broadband network. Each satellite represents a significant investment, and the company is betting heavily on its ability to deliver global mobile connectivity. However, the mounting costs associated with this endeavor raise questions about the sustainability of their business model.
stories.soWhat: As AST SpaceMobile expands, the financial strain could become a critical factor, especially if they can't deliver on their promises.

watchlist.title: Watch for SpaceX IPO chatter
watchlist.body: With recent discussions about the SpaceX secondary market, an IPO could be on the horizon, signaling a shift in investor sentiment.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on hypersonic tests
watchlist.body: The continued delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests could impact defense budgets and timelines, adding pressure to meet strategic goals.

watchlist.title: Monitor True Anomaly's growth trajectory
watchlist.body: After raising $190 million, True Anomaly's developments in co-orbital security will be pivotal for national security discussions.

watchlist.title: Expect more from the Space Force's budget
watchlist.body: With the FY27 budget adding $1.4 billion to space resilience, expect increased scrutiny on how these funds are allocated.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
